tinyhar.architecture: Original TinyHAR_Model; transformer/FC/LSTM/tnaive configuration, 20 shared filters. Adapter inserts one dimension only.
tinyhar.training: Paper Adam 1e-4, batch 256, max 150 epochs. Shared harness uses Macro-F1 early stopping (patience 15). Repository Train_baseline.py instead sets 1e-3 for its DeepConvLSTM experiment; not silently treated as TinyHAR paper setting.
differences: Released convolutions alternate strides 1,2,1,2, unlike the paper prose suggesting stride 2 throughout. Released code is retained.
Original data splits, normalization, sampling frequency and window sizes are replaced by the user-requested AutoResearcHAR protocol.

tinierhar.architecture: Original TinierHAR_Model and configs/model.yaml: 2 pooling blocks + 4 additional residual blocks, 4 initial filters, bidirectional GRU with 16 units per direction, dropout .3.
tinierhar.training: train.py: Adam .001, batch 32, 80 epochs; validation-loss plateau LR factor .1 / patience 7; early-stop patience 15. LR schedule is replayed from source-validation training during final train+val refit.
differences: Checkpoint/early-stop objective remains source-validation Macro-F1, rather than author validation loss.
Original source model constructor updates BN statistics during its dummy shape pass; retained unchanged.

bilstmattention.architecture: PyTorch port of the pinned author architecture; see research/modules/architectures/torch_author.py and bilstmattention.py.
bilstmattention.training: Published preset hyperparameters with PyTorch optimizers and source-validation checkpoint selection.
differences: PyTorch execution, initialization, dropout and optimizers differ from upstream. Reference-graph parity tests are not bundled; this does not establish benchmark reproduction.
Source-only evaluation, fixed ontology and resampling follow the project protocol.

deepconvlstmattention.architecture: Original TECO benchmark DeepConvLSTM_ATTN; no claim that TECO is the original attention paper author.
deepconvlstmattention.training: Adam .001, batch64, max150/patience15 are shared-harness choices, not a verified original attention-paper recipe.
differences: Auxiliary search alternative, not one of the supplied paper five LOSO baselines.

deepconvlstm.architecture: Four valid 5x1 convolutions followed by configurable stacked standard PyTorch nn.LSTM layers and last-time-step classification. CUDA uses the fused cuDNN recurrent implementation when available.
deepconvlstm.training: Paper batch100, RMSProp rho.9, learning rate literally printed 10e-3 (=.01), orthogonal matrix initialization and .5 dropout on dense-layer inputs. Lasagne epsilon1e-6 inside sqrt. Max300 epochs is an explicit reconstruction assumption.
differences: Standard fused LSTM replaces the reference peephole recurrence to avoid Python loops over time steps. This is an architecture adaptation, not an exact reproduction of the Lasagne graph.
Inference notebook omits dropout; paper training dropout is applied before final dense layer.
Per-gate orthogonal input/recurrent weights and zero biases are used. There are no peephole parameters. Recurrent-layer dropout is zero; configured dropout is applied before the classifier.
Checkpoints from the earlier PeepholeLSTM model use a different state-dict layout and are not directly loadable.
No claim of bit-identical optimizer/kernel results or pretrained-checkpoint compatibility.

spectra.architecture: Hann-windowed STFT magnitude; depthwise+pointwise Conv2d with BN/ReLU/residual; CxC QKV attention with gamma; temporal projection; BiGRU; attention pooling; dropout/classifier.

assumptions.reshape: Paper conv output LxFxD does not specify how to recover CxD sensor tokens. Retain C mixed feature maps, then project frequency bins to D features for each channel.

spectra.training: Paper gives2s windows/50% overlap/50Hz/standardization/cross-entropy. Adam .001, batch64, 150 epochs/patience15 are explicit assumptions; original optimizer/settings are unspecified.
differences: The SPECTRA author identifies this implementation as author code.
Parameter count and reported F1 cannot be asserted identical because key dimensions/reshape are unspecified.

source.origin: Local experimental feature-MLP implementation; no author-paper reproduction claimed

feature_mlp.architecture: Fixed per-window statistics, quantiles, autocorrelation and native-rate FFT features; source-fitted feature scaling; 256/128-unit SiLU MLP with LayerNorm and dropout.
feature_mlp.training: AdamW 1e-3, weight decay .003, batch 256, label smoothing .03; max 100 epochs and validation patience 15. Feature statistics refit only on the current training partition.
differences: Torch-native feature frontend is not checkpoint-compatible with the earlier NumPy-feature reproduction variants.
The task supplies channel names and native sampling rate. No task sampling rate, labels, splits or channel ordering are changed.
No offline target-person clustering, posture heuristics or target-fitted normalization is included.

motion_statistics.architecture: Raw, centered and bounded-standardized signal branches; 48/64-filter CNN; bidirectional 48-unit GRU with attention; 64-unit statistics branch and fused classifier.
motion_statistics.training: Adam 1e-3, batch 32, weight decay 1e-4, label smoothing .05, max 80 epochs, patience 15; validation-loss plateau LR schedule.
differences: Default first convolution stride is 2; custom_params.initial_stride=1 selects a higher temporal-resolution variant.
Defaults describe actual GRU/filter sizes rather than unused legacy custom-pipeline hidden_dim metadata.
Dataset windows, labels, preprocessing, class-weighted losses and ensembles remain separate experiment choices.

source.origin: Local slope-statistics extension; shares motion_statistics.py implementation

motion_slope.architecture: MotionAndStatistics with 8 statistics per channel, including early and late quarter-to-quarter slopes; first convolution stride 1 by default.
motion_slope.training: Shared MotionAndStatistics preset; original experiment-specific loss and LR replay are not implicitly enabled.
differences: This is an individual architecture; ensembles and their weights are configured separately.
Epoch counts and selection policies remain experiment settings, not architecture defaults.
Matching widths and stride preserve the original implementation parameter names and shapes.
